name: What special steps are needed when hanging drywall on a bathroom ceiling?

mainEntity.name: What special steps are needed when hanging drywall on a bathroom ceiling?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bathroom ceilings experience high concentrations of steam and heat, making proper board selection and ventilation vital. Installing 5/8-inch drywall or mold-resistant ceiling board prevents sagging between joists, which can happen when standard 1/2-inch drywall absorbs ambient humidity over time. Furthermore, setting the right mudding schedule is critical, as joint compound dries more slowly overhead when moisture lingers. Ensuring your bathroom exhaust fan is appropriately sized and ducted outside before ceiling drywall is hung prevents long-term moisture accumulation. After drywall finishing, sealing the ceiling with a moisture-resistant primer and quality finish paint provides an essential barrier against daily shower steam.
acceptedAnswer.description: Ceilings require sag-resistant, moisture-rated boards, properly vented exhaust fans, moisture-sealing primer, and adequate drying time between compound coats.
